title.en: Volume 54 Biographies 44: Sons of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Sons of Emperor Yuan of Liang
title.raw: 卷五十四 列傳第四十四 梁簡文帝諸子 元帝諸子 Volume 54 Biographies 44: Sons of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Sons of Emperor Yuan of Liang

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十四

translations.literal: Biography 44
translations.idiomatic: the 44th year of Biography

sentences.zh: 梁簡文帝諸子元帝諸子

translations.literal: Sons of Emperor Jianwen of Liang; Sons of Emperor Yuan of Liang
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Emperor Jianwen of Liang; The Sons of Emperor Yuan of Liang

sentences.zh: 簡文二十子。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen had twenty sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen had twenty sons.

sentences.zh: 王皇后生哀太子大器、南郡王大連。

translations.literal: Empress Wang bore the Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi and Prince Dalian of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang gave birth to the Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi and to Prince Dalian of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 陳淑容生尋陽王大心。

translations.literal: Lady Chen Shurong bore Prince Daxin of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen Shurong bore Prince Daxin of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 左夫人生南海王大臨、安陸王大春。

translations.literal: Lady Zuo bore Prince Dalin of Nanhai and Prince Dachun of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zuo bore Prince Dalin of Nanhai and Prince Dachun of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 謝夫人生瀏陽公大雅。

translations.literal: Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 張夫人生新興王大莊。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang bore Prince Dazhuang of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang bore Prince Dazhuang of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 包昭華生西陽王大鈞。

translations.literal: Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dadjun of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dadjun of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 范夫人生武甯王大威。

translations.literal: Lady Fan bore Prince Dawei of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fan bore Prince Dawei of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 褚修華生建平王大球。

translations.literal: Chu Xiuhua bore Prince Daqiu of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Xiuhua bore Prince Daqiu of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 陳夫人生義安王大昕。

translations.literal: Lady Chen bore Prince Daxin of Yian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen bore Prince Daxin of Yian.

sentences.zh: 朱夫人生綏建王大摯。

translations.literal: Lady Zhu bore Prince Dazhi of Suijian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhu bore Prince Dazhi of Suijian.

sentences.zh: 其臨川王大款、桂陽王大成、汝南王大封、樂良王大圜，並不知母氏。

translations.literal: As for Prince Dakuan of Linchuan, Prince Dacheng of Guiyang, Prince Dafeng of Runan, and Prince Dayuan of Leliang, their mothers are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dakuan of Linchuan, Prince Dacheng of Guiyang, Prince Dafeng of Runan, and Prince Dayuan of Leliang—their mothers are all unknown.

sentences.zh: 潘美人生皇子大訓，早亡無封。

translations.literal: Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Dadun, who died young without a fief.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Dadun, who died young and received no enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 其餘不知不載。

translations.literal: The rest are unknown and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder are unknown and go unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 哀太子大器字仁宗，簡文嫡長子也。

translations.literal: The Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi, style name Renzong, was Emperor Jianwen's eldest son by his principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi, styled Renzong, was the legitimate eldest son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，封宣城郡王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 太清二年十月，侯景寇建鄴，敕太子為台內大都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Taiqing, when Hou Jing raided Jianye, an edict appointed the crown prince Grand Commander within the Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Taiqing, when Hou Jing attacked Jianye, an edict named the crown prince Grand Commander within the Terrace.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，簡文即位。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, Emperor Jianwen took the throne.

sentences.zh: 六月丁亥，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai of the sixth month, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai in the sixth month he was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 大寶二年八月，景廢簡文，將害太子。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Dabao, Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen and was about to kill the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Dabao, Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen and intended to kill the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時景党稱景命召之，太子方講老子，將下床而刑人掩至。

translations.literal: At the time Jing's partisans, claiming Jing's command, summoned him; the crown prince was lecturing on the Laozi and was about to rise from his couch when executioners burst in.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's men then arrived, summoning him in Jing's name; the crown prince was expounding the Laozi and had just risen from his couch when the executioners were upon him.

sentences.zh: 太子顏色不變，徐曰：「久知此事，嗟其晚耳。」

translations.literal: The crown prince's countenance did not change, and he said slowly, "I have long known this would happen—only that it comes late."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince did not change color. He said calmly, "I have known this for a long time—it is only a pity that it comes so late."

sentences.zh: 刑者將以衣帶絞之，太子曰：「此不能見殺。」

translations.literal: The executioners were about to strangle him with a sash; the crown prince said, "That cannot be how I am put to death."
translations.idiomatic: The executioners were about to strangle him with a belt; the crown prince said, "That is not how I shall die."

sentences.zh: 乃指系帳竿下繩，命取絞之而絕。

translations.literal: He then pointed to the rope beneath the tent pole and ordered them to take it and strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to the rope tied beneath the tent pole and told them to take it and strangle him with that.

sentences.zh: 時年二十八。

translations.literal: He was then twenty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太子性寬和，兼神用端嶷，在賊中每不屈意。

translations.literal: The crown prince was by nature mild and magnanimous, and moreover of dignified bearing and keen spirit; among the rebels he never bowed his will.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was gentle and forbearing, with a dignified presence and keen intelligence; among the rebels he never bent his will.

sentences.zh: 左右竊問其故，答曰：「賊若未須見殺，雖復陵傲呵叱，其終不敢言。

translations.literal: Those about him asked in secret the reason, and he answered, "If the rebels do not yet need to kill me, even if I am overbearing and shout at them, in the end they will not dare speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants asked him privately why; he replied, "If the rebels do not yet mean to kill me, then even if I am arrogant and shout at them, they will not dare say a word in the end.

sentences.zh: 若見害時至，雖一日百拜，無益於死。」

translations.literal: If the time to be killed has come, even a hundred prostrations in a day will not help one escape death."
translations.idiomatic: But if the hour of death has come, even a hundred bows in a day will not save me from death."

sentences.zh: 問者又曰：「官今憂逼而神貌怡然，未喻此意。」

translations.literal: The questioner said again, "Your Highness is now pressed by worry, yet your spirit and bearing are serene—we do not understand this."
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "Your Highness is beset with troubles, yet your face is calm—we do not understand."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「吾自度死必在賊前，若諸叔外來，平夷羯寇，必前見殺，然後就死。

translations.literal: He answered, "I reckon for myself that death must come before the rebels; if my uncles come from outside and pacify the Jie bandits, I shall certainly be killed first and only then meet death.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am sure I must die before the rebels do. If my uncles arrive from outside and crush the Jie invaders, I shall be killed first and only then die.

sentences.zh: 若其遂開拓上流，必先見殺，後取富貴。

translations.literal: If they should open up the upper reaches, I shall still be killed first and only afterward gain wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: If they push up the Yangzi and win, I shall still be killed first and only then will others take wealth and honors.

sentences.zh: 何能以無益之愁，橫憂必死之命。」

translations.literal: How could I heap useless grief upon a fate that is sure to end in death?"
translations.idiomatic: Why should I waste useless sorrow on a life that is certain to end in death?"

sentences.zh: 景之西上，攜太子同行，及敗歸，船往往相失。

translations.literal: When Jing marched west, he took the crown prince with him; when he was defeated and returned, their boats often lost one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing marched west he took the crown prince along; on his defeat and return, their boats often lost contact.

sentences.zh: 所乘船入樅陽浦，舟中腹心並勸因此入北。

translations.literal: The boat he was on entered Zongyang Ford; the trusted men in the boat all urged that he use this chance to go north.
translations.idiomatic: His vessel entered Zongyang Ford; those closest to him aboard all urged him to seize the moment and flee north.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「自國家喪敗，志不圖生。

translations.literal: The crown prince said, "Since the state has fallen, I have no thought of living.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Since the realm has been ruined, I have no wish to live.

sentences.zh: 主上蒙塵，寧忍違離。

translations.literal: The sovereign suffers in the dust—how could I bear to leave him?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is in exile in the dust—how could I bear to abandon him?

sentences.zh: 吾今若去，乃是叛父，非謂避賊。

translations.literal: If I leave now, I would be rebelling against my father, not merely fleeing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: If I go now, I rebel against my father; I am not simply avoiding the rebels.

sentences.zh: 天下豈有無父之國。」

translations.literal: Is there a realm in the world without a father?"
translations.idiomatic: Can there be a country in the world without a father?"

sentences.zh: 便涕泗鳴咽，命即前進。

translations.literal: He then wept aloud with streaming tears and ordered them to press on at once.
translations.idiomatic: He wept aloud and ordered them to advance immediately.

sentences.zh: 賊以太子有器度，每憚之。

translations.literal: The rebels, because the crown prince had presence of mind, always feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels feared the crown prince's bearing and always held him in awe.

sentences.zh: 恐為後患，故先及禍。

translations.literal: Fearing he would be a future trouble, they brought disaster upon him first.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing future trouble, they struck at him first.

sentences.zh: 承聖元年四月，追諡哀太子，祔太廟陰室。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chengsheng, he was posthumously titled the Lamented Crown Prince and enshrined in the yin chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Chengsheng he was posthumously titled the Lamented Crown Prince and enshrined in the yin side-chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 尋陽王大心字仁恕，簡文第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Daxin of Xunyang, style name Renshu, was Emperor Jianwen's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daxin of Xunyang, styled Renshu, was the second son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰朗，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was bright and clear, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever and lucid, and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，以皇孫封當陽縣公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, as imperial grandson he was enfeoffed Duke of Dangyang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dangyang while still an imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 大同元年，為都督、郢州刺史，時年十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he became Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Yingzhou, at age thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was made Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Yingzhou, at the age of thirteen.

sentences.zh: 簡文以其幼，戒之曰：「事無大小，悉委行事。」

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen, because he was young, admonished him, saying, "In matters great or small, entrust everything to your staff officer."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen, finding him still young, warned him: "Whether the matter is great or small, leave it all to your staff officer."

sentences.zh: 大心雖不親州務，發言每合於理，眾皆驚服。

translations.literal: Though Daxin did not personally handle provincial affairs, whenever he spoke it accorded with reason, and all were astonished and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Though Daxin did not manage provincial affairs himself, his words always accorded with reason, and everyone marveled.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，為雲麾將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, he became General of the Cloudy Pennant and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing he became General of the Cloudy Pennant and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貪冒財賄，不能綏接百姓。

translations.literal: Greedy for bribes, he could not soothe and win over the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for bribes, he could not win the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 二年，侯景寇都，大心招集士卒，與上流諸軍赴援宮闕。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Hou Jing raided the capital, Daxin gathered troops and, with the armies of the upper reaches, hurried to relieve the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Hou Jing attacked the capital, Daxin raised troops and marched with the upper Yangzi armies to rescue the palace.

sentences.zh: 三年，台城陷，上甲侯蕭韶南奔宣密詔，加散騎常侍，進號平南將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year the Terrace City fell; the superior armor officer Xiao Shao fled south bearing a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Terrace City fell; Xiao Shao of the superior armor fled south with a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and given the title General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封尋陽王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 初，曆陽太守莊鐵以城降侯景，既而又奉其母來奔。

translations.literal: At first, Zhuang Tie, Administrator of Liyang, surrendered the city to Hou Jing, but afterward he brought his mother and came over to Daxin.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhuang Tie, prefect of Liyang, surrendered his city to Hou Jing, then came over with his mother.

sentences.zh: 大心以鐵舊將，厚為其禮，軍旅之事，悉以委之，以為豫章內史。

translations.literal: Daxin, because Tie was an old officer, treated him with great courtesy and entrusted all military affairs to him, appointing him Interior Governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin, knowing Tie as a veteran commander, honored him richly and entrusted all military affairs to him, making him Interior Governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 景數遣軍西上寇抄，大心輒令鐵擊破之，禽其將趙加婁，賊不能進。

translations.literal: Jing repeatedly sent armies west to raid; Daxin always had Tie defeat them and capture the general Zhao Jialou, so the rebels could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent troops west again and again to raid; Daxin had Tie repulse them each time and capture the general Zhao Jialou, so the rebels could not advance.

sentences.zh: 時鄱陽王範率眾棄合肥，屯於柵口，待援兵總集，欲俱進。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Fan of Poyang led his forces, abandoning Hefei and encamping at Shankou, waiting for relief armies to assemble before advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fan of Poyang had abandoned Hefei and camped at Shankou, waiting for all relief forces to gather before advancing together.

sentences.zh: 大心聞之，遣要範西上，以盆城處之，廩饋甚厚，欲與戮力共除禍難。

translations.literal: When Daxin heard of this, he invited Fan west, lodged him at Pencheng, supplied him generously, and wished to join forces to remove the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Daxin invited Fan west, quartered him at Pencheng, fed his troops generously, and hoped to join in removing the disaster.

sentences.zh: 會鐵據豫章反，大心令中兵參軍韋約討之，鐵敗乞降。

translations.literal: When Tie seized Yuzhang and rebelled, Daxin sent the Central Army Major Wei Yue to attack him; Tie was defeated and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Tie rebelled and held Yuzhang, Daxin sent Wei Yue to attack; Tie was defeated and begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽世子嗣先與鐵善，乃謂範曰：「昔與鐵遊處，其人才略從橫，若降江州，必不全其首領，請援之。」

translations.literal: The heir of Poyang, Sizian, was friendly with Tie and said to Fan, "In the past I associated with Tie; his talent and stratagems are resourceful—if he surrenders to Jiangzhou, his head will surely not be spared. Please rescue him."
translations.idiomatic: Sizian, heir of Poyang, was Tie's friend and told Fan, "I used to keep company with Tie—he is clever and bold. If he surrenders to Jiangzhou they will not spare his life. Please aid him."

sentences.zh: 乃遣將侯瑱救鐵，夜破韋約等營。

translations.literal: He then sent the general Hou Zhen to rescue Tie, who by night broke Wei Yue's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hou Zhen to rescue Tie, who by night smashed Wei Yue's camp.

sentences.zh: 大心大懼。

translations.literal: Daxin was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 於是二蕃釁起。

translations.literal: Thus trouble arose between the two princely domains.
translations.idiomatic: From this, strife broke out between the two princely domains.

sentences.zh: 景將任約略地至盆城，大心遣司馬韋質拒戰敗績，時帳下猶有勇士千餘人，咸說曰：「既無糧儲，難以守固，若輕騎往建州，以圖後舉，策之上也。」

translations.literal: When Jing's general Ren Yue advanced to Pencheng, Daxin sent the Marshal Wei Zhi to resist; he was defeated. There were still more than a thousand brave men in the camp, who all said, "With no grain stores, it is hard to hold firm; if we ride lightly to Jianzhou to plan a later effort, that is the best stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's general Ren Yue reached Pencheng, Daxin sent Wei Zhi to fight and was beaten. More than a thousand brave men remained in camp; all urged, "Without provisions we cannot hold—if we ride lightly to Jianzhou and plan our next move, that is best."

sentences.zh: 其母陳淑容不從，撫胸慟哭，大心乃止，遂與約和。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Chen Shurong would not agree; beating her breast she wept bitterly, and Daxin then stopped and made peace with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Chen Shurong refused; she beat her breast and wept, and Daxin halted and made peace with Yue.

sentences.zh: 二年，將遇害，遶床謂賊廂公王僧貴曰：「我以全州歸命，何忍相苦。」

translations.literal: In the second year, when he was about to be killed, he walked around the bed and said to the rebel chamberlain Wang Senggui, "I have surrendered my whole province—how can you bear to torment me so?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, about to be killed, he circled his bed and said to the rebel chamberlain Wang Senggui, "I surrendered my whole province—how can you treat me so harshly?"

sentences.zh: 乃見射而殞。

translations.literal: He was then shot and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was shot and died.

sentences.zh: 臨川王大款字仁師，簡文第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dakuan of Linchuan, style name Renshi, was Emperor Jianwen's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dakuan of Linchuan, styled Renshi, was the third son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 初封石城縣公，位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Shicheng county and held the post of Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Shicheng and served as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，簡文即位，封江夏郡王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, when Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jiangxia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing, when Emperor Jianwen took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，奔江陵，湘東王承制，改封臨川王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao he fled to Jiangling; the Prince of Xiangdong, acting on the imperial mandate, changed his fief to Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he fled to Jiangling; the Prince of Xiangdong, exercising the imperial mandate, changed his title to Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，遇害。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 南海王大臨字仁宣，簡文帝第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dalin of Nanhai, style name Renxuan, was the fourth son of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dalin of Nanhai, styled Renxuan, was the fourth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，封甯國縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningguo county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 少而敏慧。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and quick-witted.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever and quick.

sentences.zh: 年十一，遭左夫人憂，哭泣毀瘠，以孝聞。

translations.literal: At eleven he suffered the mourning for Lady Zuo; weeping he wasted away, and became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he mourned Lady Zuo, weeping until he was wasted away, and became known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 後入國學，明經射策甲科，拜中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He later entered the Imperial Academy, took first rank in the Classics examination, was appointed Secretariat Gentleman, and was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the Imperial Academy, took first rank in the Classics examination, was made Secretariat Gentleman, and promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 十一年，長兼侍中，出為琅邪、彭城二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served concurrently as Palace Attendant and went out as Prefect of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he served concurrently as Palace Attendant and went out as prefect of Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，屯端門，都督城南諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he encamped at the Duan Gate and commanded all military affairs south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, he camped at the Duan Gate and commanded all forces south of the city.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封南海郡王，出為都督、東揚州刺史，又除吳郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery, went out as Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Dongyang, and was also removed to be Prefect of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai, made Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Dongyang, and also appointed Prefect of Wu.

sentences.zh: 時張彪起義於會稽，吳人陸令公、潁川庾孟卿等勸大臨投之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Biao raised a righteous army in Kuaiji; the men of Wu, Lu Linggong and Yingchuan's Yu Mengqing, urged Dalin to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao had raised forces in Kuaiji; Lu Linggong of Wu and Yu Mengqing of Yingchuan urged Dalin to join him.

sentences.zh: 大臨曰：「彪若成功，不藉我力；

translations.literal: Dalin said, "If Biao succeeds, he will not need my strength;
translations.idiomatic: Dalin said, "If Biao succeeds, he will not need me;

sentences.zh: 如其撓敗，以我說焉，不可往也。」

translations.literal: if he is crushed and defeated, to go to him because of my words—one must not go."
translations.idiomatic: and if he is crushed, to go because I urged it—that I will not do."

sentences.zh: 二年遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was killed.

sentences.zh: 南郡王大連字仁靖，簡文第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dalian of Nankang, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dalian of Nankang, styled Renjing, was the fifth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 少俊爽，能屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was handsome and spirited, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was handsome and spirited, and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 舉止風流，雅有巧思，妙達音樂，兼善丹青。

translations.literal: His bearing was elegant, he had fine ingenuity, was masterful in music, and also excelled at painting.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was refined, he had a gift for invention, understood music deeply, and was also skilled at painting.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，封臨城縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Lincheng county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Lincheng.

sentences.zh: 七年，與南海王俱入國學，並射策甲科，皆拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered the Imperial Academy together with the Prince of Nanhai; both took top rank in the examination and were appointed Secretariat Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he and the Prince of Nanhai entered the Imperial Academy together; both took first rank and were made Secretariat Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 十年，武帝幸朱方，大連與兄大臨並從。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Emperor Wu visited Zhufang; Dalian followed together with his elder brother Dalin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Emperor Wu visited Zhufang; Dalian went with his elder brother Dalin.

sentences.zh: 武帝問曰：「汝等習騎不？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu asked, "Have you practiced riding?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "Have you practiced horsemanship?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣等未奉詔，不敢輒習。」

translations.literal: They answered, "We have not received Your Majesty's command and did not dare practice on our own."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We have not received Your Majesty's command and did not dare practice on our own."

sentences.zh: 敕令給馬試之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered horses given them for a trial.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered horses given them for a trial.

sentences.zh: 大連兄弟據鞍往還，各得馳驟之節。

translations.literal: Dalian and his brother, seated in the saddle, rode back and forth, each showing the proper pace of a gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Dalian and his brother mounted and rode back and forth, each showing proper control at the gallop.

sentences.zh: 帝大說，即賜所乘馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and at once bestowed the horses he himself rode.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and gave them the horses he had been riding.

sentences.zh: 及為啟謝，辭又甚美。

translations.literal: When they submitted a memorial of thanks, the wording was also very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorial of thanks was also beautifully worded.

sentences.zh: 帝他日謂簡文曰：「昨見大臨、大連，風韻可愛，足慰吾老年。」

translations.literal: Another day the Emperor said to Emperor Jianwen, "Yesterday I saw Dalin and Dalian—their bearing is delightful and enough to comfort me in my old age."
translations.idiomatic: Another day the Emperor told Emperor Jianwen, "Yesterday I saw Dalin and Dalian—their grace is lovely and enough to comfort me in my old age."

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，轉侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and then to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，出為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, he went out as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing he went out as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侯景入寇建鄴，大連率眾四萬來赴。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raided Jianye, Dalian led forty thousand men to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raided Jianye, Dalian led forty thousand men to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 及台城沒，援軍散還東揚州。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies scattered and he returned to Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies scattered and he returned to Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會稽豐沃，糧仗山積，東人懲景苛虐，咸樂為用，而大連恒沈湎於酒。

translations.literal: Kuaiji was fertile and rich; grain and weapons piled like mountains. The people of the east, chastened by Jing's harsh cruelty, were all glad to serve him—but Dalian constantly drowned himself in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji was fertile and rich, with grain and weapons piled like mountains. The easterners, chastened by Jing's harsh cruelty, were glad to serve him—but Dalian constantly drowned himself in wine.

sentences.zh: 宋子仙攻之，大連棄城走，追及于信安縣，大連猶醉弗之覺。

translations.literal: Song Zixian attacked him; Dalian abandoned the city and fled. Overtaken at Xin'an county, Dalian was still drunk and did not realize it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zixian attacked him; Dalian abandoned the city and fled. Overtaken at Xin'an county, Dalian was still drunk and did not realize it.

sentences.zh: 於是三吳悉為賊有。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Three Wu regions all fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Three Wu regions all fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封南郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 賊遣將趙伯超、劉神茂來攻。

translations.literal: The rebels sent the generals Zhao Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent the generals Zhao Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack.

sentences.zh: 大連專委部將留異，以城應賊，大連棄走，為賊所獲。

translations.literal: Dalian wholly entrusted affairs to his subordinate general Liu Yi, who surrendered the city to the rebels; Dalian fled in abandonment and was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Dalian wholly entrusted affairs to his subordinate general Liu Yi, who surrendered the city to the rebels; Dalian fled and was captured.

sentences.zh: 侯景以為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Hou Jing appointed him Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing appointed him Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was killed.

sentences.zh: 安陸王大春字仁經，簡文第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dachun of Anlu, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dachun of Anlu, styled Renjing, was the sixth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 少博涉書記，善吹笙。

translations.literal: In youth he was broadly versed in documents and records, and skilled at playing the sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was widely read in documents and records and skilled at the sheng flute.

sentences.zh: 天性孝謹，體貌瑰偉，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: By nature filial and cautious, his physique was magnificent and his waist belt ten arm-spans around.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial and careful; his build was imposing and his waist measured ten arm-spans.

sentences.zh: 大同六年，封西豐縣公，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Xifeng county and appointed Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Xifeng and made Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後為甯遠將軍，知石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: Later he became General Who Pacifies the Distance and supervised military affairs at the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He later became General Who Pacifies the Distance and took charge of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 侯景內寇，大春奔京口，隨邵陵王入援，戰於鍾山。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing invaded within, Dachun fled to Jingkou and followed the Prince of Shaoling in relief, fighting at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing invaded, Dachun fled to Jingkou and followed the Prince of Shaoling to the rescue, fighting at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，肥大不能行，為賊所獲。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; too stout to walk, he was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The army was beaten; too heavy to walk, he was taken by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封安陸郡王，出為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu commandery and went out as Inspector of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu and made Inspector of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 二年遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was killed.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王大成字仁和，簡文第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dacheng of Guiyang, style name Renhe, was Emperor Jianwen's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dacheng of Guiyang, styled Renhe, was the eighth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 初封新淦公。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Xingan.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，簡文即位，封山陽郡王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, when Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing, when Emperor Jianwen took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，奔江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 湘東王承制，改封桂陽王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong, acting on the imperial mandate, changed his fief to Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong, exercising the mandate, changed his title to Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 大成性甚凶粗，兼便弓馬。

translations.literal: Dacheng was by nature very fierce and coarse, and also skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was fierce and rough by nature, and also skilled with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 至江陵，被甲夜出，人謂為劫，斫之，遂失左髻。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangling, he went out at night in armor; people took him for a robber and hacked at him, and he lost the hair-knot on the left side of his head.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling he went out at night in armor; people mistook him for a bandit and struck him, so that he lost the knot of hair on his left temple.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，遇害。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 汝南王大封字仁叡，簡文第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dafeng of Runan, style name Renrui, was Emperor Jianwen's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dafeng of Runan, styled Renrui, was the ninth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 初封臨汝公。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Linru.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Linru.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，簡文即位，封宜都郡王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, when Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Yidu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing, when Emperor Jianwen took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，奔江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 湘東王承制，封汝南王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong, acting on the imperial mandate, enfeoffed him Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong, exercising the mandate, enfeoffed him Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，遇害。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 瀏陽公大雅字仁風，簡文第十二子也。

translations.literal: Duke Daya of Liyang, style name Renfeng, was Emperor Jianwen's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Daya of Liyang, styled Renfeng, was the twelfth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 大同九年，封瀏陽縣公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 少聰警，美姿儀，特為武帝所愛。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and alert, of fine bearing, and especially beloved by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever and alert, handsome in bearing, and especially loved by Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，大雅猶命左右格戰。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, Daya still ordered those about him to fight hand to hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell, Daya still ordered his men to fight at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 賊至漸眾，乃自縋而下，發憤感疾薨。

translations.literal: The rebels grew steadily more numerous; he then lowered himself by rope, and in indignant grief fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels grew in number, he let himself down by rope; stricken with grief he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 新興王大莊字仁禮，簡文第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dazhuang of Xinxing, style name Renli, was Emperor Jianwen's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dazhuang of Xinxing, styled Renli, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 性躁動。

translations.literal: His nature was restless.
translations.idiomatic: He was restless by nature.

sentences.zh: 大同九年，封高唐縣公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Gaotang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封新興郡王，位南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xinxing commandery and held the post of Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Xinxing and made Inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was killed.

sentences.zh: 西陽王大鈞字仁博，簡文第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dadjun of Xiyang, style name Renbo, was Emperor Jianwen's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dadjun of Xiyang, styled Renbo, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 性厚重，不妄戲弄。

translations.literal: His nature was weighty and steady; he did not play about rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and steady and did not play about lightly.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，武帝嘗問讀何書，對曰學詩。

translations.literal: At age seven, Emperor Wu once asked what book he was reading; he answered that he was studying the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, Emperor Wu asked what book he was reading; he said he was studying the Odes.

sentences.zh: 因令諷誦，即誦周南，音韻清雅。

translations.literal: He was therefore ordered to recite aloud, and at once recited the Zhou Nan; his tones were clear and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had him recite, and he at once recited the Zhou Nan in clear, elegant tones.

sentences.zh: 帝重之，因賜王羲之書一卷。

translations.literal: The Emperor valued him and bestowed a scroll of Wang Xizhi's calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor prized him and gave him a scroll of Wang Xizhi's writing.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封西陽郡王，位丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang commandery and held the post of Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang and made Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 二年，監揚州，遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he supervised Yangzhou and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he supervised Yangzhou and was killed.

sentences.zh: 武甯王大威字仁容，簡文第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dawei of Wuning, style name Renrong, was Emperor Jianwen's fifteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dawei of Wuning, styled Renrong, was the fifteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，眉目如畫。

translations.literal: His bearing was fine; his brows and eyes were like a painting.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was elegant; his brows and eyes were like a painting.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封武甯郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 二年，為丹陽尹，遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he became Governor of Danyang and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became Governor of Danyang and was killed.

sentences.zh: 皇子大訓字仁德，簡文第十六子也。

translations.literal: The imperial son Dadun, style name Rende, was Emperor Jianwen's sixteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son Dadun, styled Rende, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 少而腳疾，不敢躡履。

translations.literal: From youth he had an ailment of the feet and did not dare tread in shoes.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he had a foot ailment and dared not wear shoes.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，未封而亡，年十歲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, before he was enfeoffed he died, at age ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing he died before enfeoffment, at the age of ten.

sentences.zh: 建平王大球字仁玉，簡文帝第十七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Daqiu of Jianping, style name Renyu, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daqiu of Jianping, styled Renyu, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封建平郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 性明慧夙成。

translations.literal: His nature was bright and clever from early youth.
translations.idiomatic: He was bright and clever from early childhood.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景圍台城，武帝素歸心釋教，每發誓願，恒云：「若有眾生應受諸苦，衍身代當。」

translations.literal: At first, when Hou Jing besieged the Terrace City, Emperor Wu had long turned his heart to Buddhism; whenever he made a vow he always said, "If there are living beings who ought to suffer every pain, let Yan take their place."
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing first besieged the Terrace City, Emperor Wu had long devoted himself to Buddhism; whenever he made a vow he would say, "If any living being must suffer every pain, let me take it in their stead."

sentences.zh: 時大球年甫七歲，聞而驚謂母曰：「官家尚爾，兒安敢辭。」

translations.literal: At the time Daqiu was only seven; hearing this he was startled and said to his mother, "If the sovereign is still like this, how dare his son refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Daqiu was then only seven; startled, he told his mother, "If the Emperor is still like this, how dare I refuse?"

sentences.zh: 乃六時禮佛，亦云：「凡有眾生應獲苦報，悉大球代受。」

translations.literal: He then worshiped the Buddha at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever living beings ought to receive the report of suffering, let Daqiu take it all."
translations.idiomatic: He then worshiped at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever suffering living beings must receive, let Daqiu take it all."

sentences.zh: 其早慧如此。

translations.literal: His precocity was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his precocity.

sentences.zh: 二年遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was killed.

sentences.zh: 義安王大昕字仁朗，簡文帝第十八子也。

translations.literal: Prince Daxin of Yian, style name Renlang, was Emperor Jianwen's eighteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daxin of Yian, styled Renlang, was the eighteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 年四歲，母陳夫人卒，便哀毀有若成人，晨夕涕泣，眼為之傷。

translations.literal: At four years old, when his mother Lady Chen died, he grieved and wasted away as though an adult, weeping morning and evening until his eyes were injured.
translations.idiomatic: At four, when his mother Lady Chen died, he grieved and wasted away like an adult, weeping morning and evening until his eyes were injured.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，大昕奉慰簡文，嗚噎不自勝，左右莫不掩泣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Daxin came to console Emperor Jianwen, sobbing beyond control; those beside him none failed to cover their faces and weep.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, Daxin came to console Emperor Jianwen, sobbing uncontrollably; none beside him failed to cover their faces and weep.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，封義安郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yian.

sentences.zh: 二年遇害。

translations.literal: In the second year he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was killed.

sentences.zh: 綏建王大摯字仁瑛，簡文第十九子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dazhi of Suijian, style name Renying, was Emperor Jianwen's nineteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dazhi of Suijian, styled Renying, was the nineteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 幼雄壯有膽氣，及台城陷，乃歎曰：「大丈夫會當滅虜屬。」

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and had courage; when the Terrace City fell he sighed and said, "A true man will surely wipe out these barbarian thralls."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was bold and spirited; when the Terrace City fell he sighed, "A real man will one day destroy these barbarian vermin."

sentences.zh: 奶媼驚掩其口，曰：「勿妄言，禍將及。」

translations.literal: His nurse, startled, covered his mouth and said, "Do not speak rashly—disaster will come."
translations.idiomatic: His nurse, alarmed, clapped her hand over his mouth and said, "Do not speak rashly—disaster is near."

sentences.zh: 大摯笑曰：「禍至非由此。」

translations.literal: Dazhi laughed and said, "When disaster comes, it will not be because of this."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhi laughed and said, "When disaster comes, it will not be from this."

sentences.zh: 大寶元年封，二年遇害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed; in the second year he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Dabao and killed in the second.

sentences.zh: 樂良王大圜，簡文第二十子也。

translations.literal: Prince Dayuan of Leliang was Emperor Jianwen's twentieth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dayuan of Leliang was the twentieth son of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Dabao.

sentences.zh: 後入周。

translations.literal: Later he entered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went over to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋位內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Sui he held the post of Secretariat Vice-Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as Secretariat Vice-Minister.

sentences.zh: 元帝諸子。

translations.literal: The sons of Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 徐妃生武烈世子方等。

translations.literal: Consort Xu bore the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xu bore the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng.

sentences.zh: 王貴嬪生貞惠世子方諸、始安王方略。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Wang bore the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu and Prince Fanglue of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Wang bore the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu and Prince Fanglue of Shian.

sentences.zh: 袁貴人生湣懷太子方矩。

translations.literal: Honored Lady Yuan bore the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Lady Yuan bore the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju.

sentences.zh: 夏貴妃生敬皇帝。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Xia bore Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Xia bore Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 自餘不顯。

translations.literal: The rest are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 武烈世子方等字實相，元帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng, style name Shixiang, was Emperor Yuan's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng, styled Shixiang, was the eldest son of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，有俊才，善騎射，尤長巧思。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, had outstanding talent, was skilled at riding and shooting, and especially excelled in ingenious contrivances.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was clever and keen, gifted and skilled at riding and archery, and especially ingenious.

sentences.zh: 性愛林泉，特好散逸。

translations.literal: By nature he loved forests and springs and was especially fond of untrammeled ease.
translations.idiomatic: He loved forests and streams by nature and especially favored a life of ease.

sentences.zh: 嘗著論曰：「人生處世，如白駒過隙耳。

translations.literal: He once wrote a discourse, saying, "Life in the world is like a white colt flashing past a crack in the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a treatise: "Life in the world is like a white colt flashing past a crack in the wall.

sentences.zh: 一壺之酒，足以養性，一簞之食，足以怡形。

translations.literal: A pot of wine is enough to nourish one's nature; a basket of food is enough to delight one's form.
translations.idiomatic: A pot of wine is enough to nourish the nature; a basket of food is enough to please the body.

sentences.zh: 生在蒿蓬，死葬溝壑，瓦棺石槨，何以異茲。

translations.literal: Born amid artemisia and fleabane, buried in ditches and gullies—tile coffin or stone sarcophagus, how do they differ from this?
translations.idiomatic: Born in the weeds, buried in a ditch—a tile coffin or a stone sarcophagus, what difference is there?

sentences.zh: 吾嘗夢為魚，因化為鳥。

translations.literal: I once dreamed I was a fish and thereby became a bird.
translations.idiomatic: I once dreamed I was a fish, and then became a bird.

sentences.zh: 方其夢也，何樂如之，及其覺也，何憂斯類，良由吾之不及魚鳥者遠矣。

translations.literal: While dreaming, what joy could equal it; when awake, what sorrow of this kind—truly because I fall far short of fish and birds.
translations.idiomatic: While dreaming, what joy could match it; when I woke, what sorrow—because I am so far beneath fish and birds.

sentences.zh: 故魚鳥飛浮，任其志性，吾之進退，恒在掌握。

translations.literal: Thus fish and birds fly and float, following their natures; my coming and going are always in another's grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Fish and birds fly and float as their natures dictate; my comings and goings are always in another's hand.

sentences.zh: 舉首懼觸，搖足恐墮。

translations.literal: I raise my head fearing I will strike something; I move my foot fearing I will fall.
translations.idiomatic: I lift my head in fear of striking something; I shift my foot in fear of falling.

sentences.zh: 若使吾終得與魚鳥同遊，則去人間如脫屣耳。」

translations.literal: If I could at last roam with fish and birds, I would leave the human world as though casting off shoes."
translations.idiomatic: If I could roam with fish and birds at last, I would leave the human world as easily as kicking off shoes."

sentences.zh: 初，徐妃以嫉妒失寵，方諸母王氏以冶容幸嬖。

translations.literal: At first Consort Xu lost favor through jealousy; Fangzhu's mother Lady Wang, with her seductive beauty, won intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: At first Consort Xu lost favor through jealousy; Fangzhu's mother Lady Wang, with her alluring looks, won the Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 及王夫人終，元帝歸咎徐妃，方等意不自安。

translations.literal: When Lady Wang died, Emperor Yuan blamed Consort Xu; Fangdeng felt ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wang died, Emperor Yuan blamed Consort Xu; Fangdeng grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞之，又惡方等，方等益懼，故述此論以申其志。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of it, he disliked Fangdeng still more; Fangdeng grew still more afraid, and therefore set forth this discourse to declare his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan heard of it and disliked Fangdeng still more; Fangdeng grew more afraid and wrote this treatise to declare his mind.

sentences.zh: 時武帝年高，欲見諸王長子。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wu was advanced in years and wished to see the eldest sons of the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was then old and wished to see each prince's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 元帝遣方等，方等欣然升舟，冀免憂辱。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan sent Fangdeng; Fangdeng gladly boarded the boat, hoping to escape worry and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan sent Fangdeng; Fangdeng gladly boarded the boat, hoping to escape distress and shame.

sentences.zh: 行至繇水，遇侯景亂，元帝召之，方等啟曰：「昔申生不愛其死，方等豈顧其生。」

translations.literal: When he reached the Yao River he met Hou Jing's rebellion; Emperor Yuan summoned him, and Fangdeng reported, "In the past Shen Sheng did not value his life—how should Fangdeng care for his?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Yao River he met Hou Jing's rebellion; Emperor Yuan recalled him, and Fangdeng wrote, "Long ago Shen Sheng did not cling to life—why should Fangdeng cling to his?"

sentences.zh: 元帝省書歎息，知無還意，乃配步騎一萬，使援台城。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan read the report, sighed, knew he had no wish to return, and then assigned him ten thousand foot and horse to relieve the Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan read it, sighed, knew he would not return, and gave him ten thousand foot and horse to relieve the Terrace City.

sentences.zh: 賊每來攻，方等必身當矢石。

translations.literal: Whenever the rebels came to attack, Fangdeng always placed himself in the path of arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the rebels attacked, Fangdeng always placed himself in the path of arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 城陷，方等歸荊州，收集士馬，甚得眾和。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Fangdeng returned to Jingzhou, gathered soldiers and horses, and won the people's hearts exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he returned to Jingzhou, gathered troops and horses, and won great support among the people.

sentences.zh: 元帝始歎其能。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan began to admire his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan began to admire his ability.

sentences.zh: 方等又勸修築城柵，以備不虞，既成，樓雉相望，周回七十餘里。

translations.literal: Fangdeng also urged building city palisades against the unexpected; when finished, towers and battlements faced one another, the circuit more than seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdeng also urged building palisades against surprise; when done, towers and battlements faced one another for more than seventy li around.

sentences.zh: 元帝觀之甚說，入謂徐妃曰：「若更有一子如此，吾復何憂。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan viewed them with great pleasure and went in to tell Consort Xu, "If I had another son like this, what would I have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan viewed them with delight and told Consort Xu, "If I had another son like this, what would I have to fear?"

sentences.zh: 徐妃不答，垂泣而退。

translations.literal: Consort Xu did not answer; weeping, she withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xu did not answer; weeping, she withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元帝忿之，因疏其穢行牓於大合，方等入見，益以自危。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was angry at this and therefore posted a bill of her shameful conduct in the great hall; when Fangdeng came in to see him, he felt still more endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was angry and posted a bill of her shameful conduct in the great hall; when Fangdeng came to audience, he felt still more endangered.

sentences.zh: 時河東王為湘州刺史，不受令。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Hedong was Inspector of Xiangzhou and did not accept orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hedong was then Inspector of Xiangzhou and would not obey orders.

sentences.zh: 方等求征之，元帝謂曰：「汝有水厄，深宜慎之。」

translations.literal: Fangdeng asked to campaign against him; Emperor Yuan said to him, "You have a water calamity in your fate—you must be deeply cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Fangdeng asked to campaign against him; Emperor Yuan said, "You have a water doom in your fate—you must be very careful."

sentences.zh: 拜為都督，令南討。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-chief and ordered to campaign south.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commander-in-chief and ordered south.

sentences.zh: 方等臨行謂所親曰：「吾此段出征，必死無二，死而獲所，吾豈愛生。」

translations.literal: On the eve of departure Fangdeng told those close to him, "On this campaign I am certain to die without alternative; if I die and gain my goal, how should I love life?"
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out he told his intimates, "On this campaign I am sure to die; if I die and gain my aim, why should I cling to life?"

sentences.zh: 及至麻溪，軍敗溺死，求屍不得。

translations.literal: When he reached Maxi the army was defeated and he drowned; his corpse could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: At Maxi the army was beaten and he drowned; his body could not be found.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞之心喜，不以為戚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of it, his heart rejoiced and he did not regard it as grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan heard, he was secretly glad and did not grieve.

sentences.zh: 後追思其才，贈侍中、中軍將軍、揚州刺史，諡忠壯世子，並招魂以葬之。

translations.literal: Later, recalling his talent, he posthumously granted him Palace Attendant, General of the Central Army, and Inspector of Yangzhou, titled the Loyal and Martial Heir Apparent, and buried him by summoning his soul.
translations.idiomatic: Later, remembering his ability, he posthumously made him Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army, Inspector of Yangzhou, titled him the Loyal and Martial Heir Apparent, and buried him by summoning his soul.

sentences.zh: 方等注范曄後漢書，未就。

translations.literal: Fangdeng annotated Fan Ye's Book of the Later Han but did not finish.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdeng had begun annotating Fan Ye's Book of the Later Han but did not finish.

sentences.zh: 所撰三十國春秋及篤靜子行於世。

translations.literal: His Spring and Autumn of the Thirty States and his Dutiful Tranquility Master circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Spring and Autumn of the Thirty States and Dutiful Tranquility Master circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 元帝即位，改諡武烈世子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he changed the posthumous title of the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he changed the posthumous title of the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 封子莊為永嘉王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his son Zhuang as Prince of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his son Zhuang as Prince of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 及魏克江陵，莊年甫七歲，為人家所匿。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, Zhuang was only seven years old and was hidden in a common household.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei captured Jiangling, Zhuang was only seven years old and was hidden in a common household.

sentences.zh: 後王琳迎送建鄴。

translations.literal: Later Wang Lin welcomed him and escorted him to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Lin welcomed him and escorted him to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 及敬帝立，出質于齊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing was established, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing was established, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi.

sentences.zh: 敬帝太平二年，陳武帝將受禪，王琳請莊于齊以主梁嗣，自盆城濟江。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping under Emperor Jing, as Chen Wudi was about to accept the abdication, Wang Lin requested Zhuang from Qi to head the Liang succession, and crossed the river from Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping under Emperor Jing, as Chen Wudi was about to accept the abdication, Wang Lin requested Zhuang from Qi to head the Liang succession and crossed the river from Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，即帝位於郢州，年號天啟，置百官。

translations.literal: In the second month he took the throne at Yingzhou, reign era Tianqi, and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi, and established the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 王琳總其軍國。

translations.literal: Wang Lin directed all military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin directed all military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，莊為陳人所敗，其御史中丞劉仲威奉以奔壽陽，遂入齊。

translations.literal: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men; his Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei escorted him in flight to Shouyang, and he then entered Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men; his Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei escorted him in flight to Shouyang, and he then entered Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊武平元年，授特進、開府儀同三司，封梁王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master with Opens Office and Parallels in Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master with Opens Office and Parallels in Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 齊朝許以興復，竟不果而齊亡，莊在鄴飲氣而死。

translations.literal: The court of Qi promised restoration of Liang, but in the end it did not come to pass; Qi perished, and Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.
translations.idiomatic: The court of Qi promised restoration of Liang, but in the end it did not come to pass; Qi perished, and Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.

sentences.zh: 貞惠世子方諸字明智，元帝第二子也。

translations.literal: The Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu, style name Mingzhi, was Emperor Yuan's second son.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu, styled Mingzhi, was the second son of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 幼聰警博學，明老、易，善談玄，風采清越，特為元帝所愛，母王氏又有寵。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever, alert, and broadly learned; he mastered the Laozi and Changes, was skilled at discussing the abstruse, his bearing clear and surpassing, and was especially loved by Emperor Yuan; his mother Lady Wang also enjoyed favor.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever, widely learned, versed in the Laozi and Changes, skilled at metaphysical discourse, of refined bearing, and especially beloved by Emperor Yuan; his mother Lady Wang was also favored.

sentences.zh: 及方等敗後，元帝謂曰：「不有所廢，其何以興。

translations.literal: After Fangdeng's defeat, Emperor Yuan said to him, "Unless something is cast aside, how can anything rise?
translations.idiomatic: After Fangdeng's defeat, Emperor Yuan told him, "Unless something is discarded, how can anything arise?

sentences.zh: 勿以汝兄為念。」

translations.literal: Do not brood on your elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Do not dwell on your elder brother."

sentences.zh: 因拜中撫軍將軍以自副。

translations.literal: He was then appointed General of the Central Pacification Army as the Emperor's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made General of the Central Pacification Army as the Emperor's deputy.

sentences.zh: 又出為郢州刺史，鎮江夏，以鮑泉為行事。

translations.literal: He also went out as Inspector of Yingzhou, garrisoned Jiangxia, and Bao Quan served as his staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Inspector of Yingzhou, stationed at Jiangxia, with Bao Quan as his executive officer.

sentences.zh: 時元帝遣徐文盛與侯景將任約相持，方諸年十五，童心未革，恃文盛在近，不恤軍政，日與鮑泉蒱酒為樂。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Yuan sent Xu Wensheng to contend with Hou Jing's general Ren Yue; Fangzhu was fifteen, his childish heart not yet changed, relying on Wensheng being near and heedless of military affairs, daily drinking and gambling with Bao Quan for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan had sent Xu Wensheng to hold Ren Yue, Hou Jing's general; Fangzhu was fifteen, still a boy, trusting that Wensheng was near and neglecting military affairs, passing his days drinking and gambling with Bao Quan.

sentences.zh: 侯景知之，乃遣其將宋子仙從間道襲之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing learned of this, he sent his general Song Zixian to strike by a hidden route.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing learned of this and sent Song Zixian by a secret path to attack.

sentences.zh: 百姓奔告，方諸與鮑泉並不信，曰：「文盛大軍在下，虜安得來？」

translations.literal: The common people ran to report it; Fangzhu and Bao Quan both disbelieved, saying, "Wensheng's great army is below—how could the barbarians come?"
translations.idiomatic: The people came with urgent news; Fangzhu and Bao Quan would not believe them: "Wensheng's main force is downstream—how could the enemy get here?"

sentences.zh: 始命閉門，賊已入城。

translations.literal: Only then did he order the gates closed—the rebels were already inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he order the gates shut—the rebels were already in the city.

sentences.zh: 方諸方踞泉腹，以五色毦辮其須。

translations.literal: Fangzhu was just sitting astride Bao Quan's belly, braiding his beard with five-colored wool.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzhu was sprawled on Bao Quan's belly, braiding his beard with colored wool.

sentences.zh: 子仙執方諸以歸。

translations.literal: Zixian seized Fangzhu and took him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian seized Fangzhu and carried him off.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯軍至蔡洲，景遂害之。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian's army reached Caizhou, Jing then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian's army reached Caizhou, Hou Jing killed him.

sentences.zh: 元帝追諡貞惠世子。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan posthumously titled him the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan posthumously titled him the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子方矩字德規，元帝第四子也。

translations.literal: The Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju, style name Degui, was Emperor Yuan's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju, styled Degui, was the fourth son of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 少勤學，美容止。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently and had handsome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied diligently and had handsome bearing.

sentences.zh: 初封南安侯。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 太清初，累遷侍中，中衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing he rose in succession to Palace Attendant and General of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiqing he rose in succession to Palace Attendant and General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，拜王太子，改名元良。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan acted under imperial mandate, he appointed him princely heir and changed his name to Yuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan acted under imperial mandate, he appointed him princely heir and changed his name to Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 承聖元年十一月丙子，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Chengsheng 1, on the day bingzi, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Chengsheng 1, on the day bingzi, he was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及升儲位，昵狎群下，好著微服。

translations.literal: Once he ascended the heir's position, he was intimate with his subordinates and liked to wear plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ascended the heir's position, he was intimate with his subordinates and liked to wear plain dress.

sentences.zh: 嘗入朝，公服中著碧絲布袴，摳衣高，元帝見之大怪，遣尚書周弘正責之，因使太子師弘正。

translations.literal: Once when he came to court in official dress he wore blue silk cloth trousers inside, hiking up his robe high; Emperor Yuan saw it and was greatly shocked. He sent Minister of the Masters of Writing Zhou Hongzheng to rebuke him, and made Hongzheng the crown prince's tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he came to court in official dress he wore blue silk trousers inside, hiking up his robe high; Emperor Yuan was greatly shocked, sent Minister of the Masters of Writing Zhou Hongzheng to rebuke him, and made Hongzheng the crown prince's tutor.

sentences.zh: 佗日，弘正謁見，元帝問曰：「太子比頗受卿導不？」

translations.literal: Another day, when Hongzheng had an audience, Emperor Yuan asked: "Has the crown prince lately been guided by you much?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day, when Hongzheng had an audience, Emperor Yuan asked, "Has the crown prince lately been guided by you much?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「太子聖德乃未極日新，幸無大過。」

translations.literal: He answered: "The crown prince's sacred virtue has not yet reached perfection day by day; fortunately there are no great faults."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The crown prince's sacred virtue has not yet reached perfection day by day; fortunately there are no great faults."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿以我父子故未直言，從容之間，無失和嶠之對。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Because we are father and son you did not speak plainly; in your composed reply, you failed to match He Qiao's answer."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Because we are father and son you did not speak plainly; in your composed reply, you failed to match He Qiao's answer."

sentences.zh: 便有廢立計。

translations.literal: He then formed a plan to depose and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He then formed a plan to depose and replace him.

sentences.zh: 未及行而江陵喪亡，遇害。

translations.literal: Before it could be carried out Jiangling was lost and destroyed, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before it could be carried out Jiangling was lost and destroyed, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 太子聰穎凶暴猜忍，俱有元帝風。

translations.literal: The crown prince was clever, fierce, violent, and cruelly suspicious—all in Emperor Yuan's manner.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was clever, fierce, violent, and cruelly suspicious—all in Emperor Yuan's manner.

sentences.zh: 敬帝承制，追諡湣懷太子。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing, acting under imperial mandate, posthumously titled him the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, acting under imperial mandate, posthumously titled him the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 始安王方略，元帝第十子，貞惠世子母弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Fanglue of Shian was Emperor Yuan's tenth son, the younger brother by the same mother as the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fanglue of Shian was Emperor Yuan's tenth son and the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 母王氏，王琳之次姊，元帝即位，拜貴嬪，次妹又為良人，並蒙寵倖，方略益鍾愛。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Wang, the second elder sister of Wang Lin; when Emperor Yuan ascended the throne she was made Honored Consort, and her younger sister was also made Honored Lady; both enjoyed favor, and Fanglue was especially cherished.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Wang was Wang Lin's second elder sister; when Emperor Yuan took the throne she became Honored Consort, and her younger sister became Honored Lady; both were favored, and Fanglue was especially doted on.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，元帝結好于魏，方略年數歲便遣入關。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan sought friendship with Wei and, when Fanglue was only a few years old, sent him into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan sought ties with Wei and sent Fanglue into the passes while he was still a small child.

sentences.zh: 元帝親送近畿，執手歔欷，既而旋駕憶之，賦詩曰：「如何吾幼子，勝衣已別離，十日無由宴，千里送遠垂。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan personally escorted him to the near suburbs, took his hand and sobbed; afterward, as he turned his carriage back he thought of him and composed a poem: "How is it with my little son—already past the age of short coats and parted from me; ten days without a feast together, a thousand li sending him off in tears."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan escorted him to the suburbs himself, took his hand and wept; turning back he missed him and wrote: "How is it with my little son—already in short coats and parted from me; ten days without a shared meal, a thousand li seeing him off in tears."

sentences.zh: 至長安即得還，贈遺甚厚。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an he was allowed to return at once; the gifts sent back were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an he was soon allowed to return; the gifts sent back were lavish.

sentences.zh: 江陵喪亡，遇害。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪、良人並更誕子，未出合，無封失名。

translations.literal: The Honored Consort and Honored Lady each bore sons again; they had not yet left the palace quarters, received no fiefs, and their names are lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Honored Consort and Honored Lady each bore more sons; they had not yet left the inner quarters, received no titles, and their names are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 論曰：簡文提挈寇戎，元帝崎嶇危亂，諸子之備踐艱棘，蓋時運之所鍾乎。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Emperor Jianwen led the realm through invaders; Emperor Yuan struggled through peril and chaos—the sons' full share of hardship and thorn—was this not what the times had allotted?
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Emperor Jianwen bore the realm through invasion; Emperor Yuan struggled through danger and chaos—the sons' full measure of hardship—was this not the allotment of the age?

sentences.zh: 武烈以幹蠱之材，居塚嗣之任，竟亦當年擯落，通塞亦云命也，哀哉！

translations.literal: The Martial and Fierce heir, with talent fit to stem disaster, held the charge of the heir in the tomb-line—yet in the end he was cast aside that same year; fortune and misfortune, too, are said to be fate. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The Martial and Fierce heir had talent to stem ruin and bore the heir's charge—yet that very year he was cast aside; rise and fall are also called fate. Alas!
